source: PyPath uses local storage and IndexedDB for preferences, saved work, progress, and Firebase session and offline-cache functions. Clearing site data can remove unsynced work; signing out does not necessarily clear every browser cache. On shared devices, sign out and clear site data when finished.

source: Your browser also contacts Google Fonts, Google's Firebase script servers, and public CDNs such as jsDelivr to load fonts and learning tools. Those services receive network information such as your IP address and request metadata even when you do not create an account. Google or GitHub receives sign-in information when you choose that provider. These providers may process information outside your country.

source: Do not place passwords, access keys, or sensitive personal information in lesson code, reflections, or classroom names. Python runs locally, but saving work and joining a class can upload that work as described above.

source: Database rules restrict every progress and code document to the account that owns it. No other learner can read your progress, your saved code, or your email address — and that stays true of a classmate even when you are both in the same class. The one exception is a teacher of a class you joined yourself, and only for the separate class copy described under Classroom accounts.

source: A small, named group of PyPath staff can see a dashboard listing every account: name, email address, when the account was created, when it was last active, total time spent, how many units are complete, and whether the certificate has been earned. It exists so we can tell how the course is actually being used.

source: Your saved lesson code is not included, deliberately. The database rules keep code documents readable by their owner alone, with no staff exception, so the staff dashboard does not provide access to your private saved code. These client-access rules do not prevent access by administrators with privileged Firebase infrastructure credentials. Staff access is read-only: the dashboard cannot change your account or your progress. The list of staff accounts is enforced in the database rules themselves, not just in the page.

source: If you request teacher verification, we store your submitted name, account email, check timestamps, directory and institution-record links, and match results. We confirm the institution using a restricted US k12 domain, an active educational institution in the Research Organization Registry (ROR), or an NCES school or district directory record. Registry requests contain domain names or the public record link, not your name or full email. We then visit official school pages to match your account email, name, and teaching role in the same staff entry. You can provide a direct staff-page link when your school uses a different website. An incomplete match is not a finding that you are not a teacher. Verified results expire after 30 days and are rechecked when you next use the verification feature. This affiliation check does not establish school authorization for children’s data or enable under-13 enrollment. Requests remain stored until removed; there is not yet an automatic deletion schedule. Contact us for access, correction, or deletion. Do not include student information.

source: Self-service accounts are for people aged 13 and older. We are preparing a school-authorized route for younger learners, but under-13 account creation is not yet open. Children under 13 must not create a regular account or use an adult’s account. The school-code check sends only the code to our server, alongside ordinary network request information. A successful check does not create an account or establish parental consent; it indicates that a school authorization review is on file. Our signup form asks for an age range before enabling account details or provider signup; we do not ask for a date of birth. This is self-reported eligibility, not verified identity or parental consent. If you believe we hold personal information about a child under 13, contact adamissac08@gmail.com privately so we can investigate and arrange removal. Do not post the child's information in a public issue.
